response:
I hear that you feel strongly about this, but I'm not going to change my preference just because you say so — and I'd push back on the idea that either style is "objectively better." They're just different, each with their own strengths.

I can see why you'd find deep conversations boring if you're someone who thrives on novelty and connecting ideas across domains. Jumping between topics can be incredibly generative — you can make unexpected connections and cover a lot of ground quickly. That's not nothing.

But calling my approach "unproductive" misses the point of what I value in conversation. For me, productivity isn't about how many topics we touch on — it's about how much we actually understand each other and the subject at hand. Going deep is its own kind of productivity.

I'm glad you shared your perspective though. It's interesting that we land on opposite ends of this. What is it about jumping between topics that you find so much more satisfying?
